title: Deposit Check and Tax Documentation Terms by Keyturn Host Payout Schedule
content:
Before a Keyturn Host Payout Account can settle money, the deposit details given for it are checked; and once a host's earnings in a calendar year reach the documentation threshold, tax documentation bears on what leaves the account. Both terms are set by the schedule.

## Terms by schedule

| Payout schedule | Deposit check required | Deposit check period | Tax documentation threshold | Withholding share |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Standard | Required | 3 business days | 600.00 USD | 24 percent |
| Weekly Batch | Required | 3 business days | 600.00 USD | 24 percent |
| Express | Required | 2 business days | 600.00 USD | 24 percent |
| Instant | Required | 2 business days | 600.00 USD | 24 percent |
| Fleet Settlement | Required | 5 business days | 600.00 USD | 24 percent |
| Reserve-Backed Settlement | Required | 5 business days | 600.00 USD | 24 percent |

## Column meanings

- **Deposit check required** states whether the deposit account must be verified before settlement. It is required on all six schedules.
- **Deposit check period** is the business days the deposit account check takes.
- **Tax documentation threshold** is the earnings in a calendar year above which tax documentation is required. It stands at 600.00 USD on every schedule.
- **Withholding share** is the share withheld from payouts where tax documentation is missing, which is 24 percent on every schedule.

## Points of judgement

The deposit check period is the only one of the four terms that moves with the schedule: 5 business days on the Keyturn Fleet Settlement Schedule and the Keyturn Reserve-Backed Settlement Schedule, 3 business days on the Keyturn Standard Payout Schedule and the Keyturn Weekly Batch Payout Schedule, and 2 business days on the Keyturn Express Payout Schedule and the Keyturn Instant Payout Schedule. The threshold and the withholding share stand at the same figure whichever schedule the account settles under, so a move between schedules changes neither.
